html:
The Wahpeton ("dwellers among the leaves") are one of the four bands of the Santee, or Eastern Dakota, a division of the Oceti Sakowin or Seven Council Fires. In the 1600s and 1700s they lived in the woods and prairies of what is now Minnesota.

They hunted, gathered wild rice, fished and grew some maize, and moved between summer villages and winter camps. They traded furs with the French and later the British. Treaties in 1851 forced them onto a narrow reservation along the Minnesota River. After the Dakota War of 1862 they were expelled from Minnesota. Many Wahpeton now belong to the Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate of South Dakota, along with the Sisseton, or to reserves in Canada. Their close kin include the Mdewakanton.
